transcript.text: I have over 100 plus sales people who
work for me across our portfolio that
does over $250 million a year. These are
five rules for closing that I teach
them. Number one, the person asking the
question is always in control and you
want that to be you. Number two, be like
smoke. If you don't know how to answer
it, just ask a question about their
question. Number three, tell them what
their question means. They [music] might
say, "I need to think about it." And you
might say, "That's amazing. That's what
some of our best customers have asked.
What's your main concern?" And so
instead of taking a step back, they
actually take a step forward in the
sale. Rule number four, use straw men
for harsh truth. If you have a hard
truth that you want to ask or a question
that can seem kind of cutting, you don't
want to ask it to them. You want to tell
them a story of someone just like them
that you ask the question to and then
you have a third party in the sale who
can then be the person you deliver the
hard truth to and then they just bear
witness. Five, [music] retain childlike
curiosity at all times. And so if you
say, "Huh, that's interesting." Or,
"Huh, that's a really good question."
That then keeps you in the sale. It
keeps [music] rapport.
